label: Descent with slots of at least a fixed positive length
definition: SlotsAtLeast k c holds when some real delta > 0 bounds every slot between consecutive members of the sequence from below: delta <= reading (c n) - reading (c (n + 1)) for all n. With Descent c it is a spaced descent: stations back in time, each slot lasting at least delta (for example one station per past day). Counterexample: t, t/2, t/4, ... is a descent whose slots shrink to zero, so it is not spaced. A spaced descent from t exists exactly when, in linear time, the past of t is metrically infinite (unboundedOfSpaced and spacedDescentOfUnbounded), and in linear time every spaced descent is coinitial (coinitialOfSpaced).
note: Analyst metric definition; attribution deferred. Slot length is measured by the supplied clock, and the intended reading uses the privileged clock (CLOCK_1, CLOCK disambiguation 725f3417-73d0-489f-b8ab-7b2628ff36b7): slots of at least delta are then room for a duplicate of one station patch lasting at most delta. It is the metric restriction that the order-theoretic Coinitial lacks: coinitial descents may accumulate metrically (t/2^n in (0, t]), spaced ones may not. delta is existentially quantified per descent, not fixed in advance; the derivation uses only slots of length at least one clock unit.
